evidence: Swap test FAIL: a council allotment-plot booking or a bike-hire shop could take the frame unchanged (white masthead with a small glyph and the name in bold body type, pale ground, white bordered cards in a 2-up grid, one dark-green filled button, green 'Available' badges). Only the copy (deposit, sessions, 'Open' days, volunteers, 14 Mill Lane) is bound to Fernhill.

Category-guess test FAIL: predicted default for a community/civic booking flow is a GOV.UK-like pale ground, one sober green or teal accent, bordered cards, an error summary box with red border, a single sans; this matches find, basket (errors) and confirm almost element for element. Nothing reads as the predictable opposite either; it simply is the default.

Similar-prompt test FAIL: 'a seed library's online reservation for members who collect at a weekly stall' would plausibly produce the same green restrained palette, card grid with icon thumbnails, calendar day picker and session radio cards.

Identity-carrying elements are thin: the mark is a generic wrench line icon plus 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type (items-ladder-3m/default/1280-light.png, top left); every tool thumbnail is the same wrench in a pale green square (10 cards), so no imagery carries the library's stock.

Nearest thing to a signature is the pick-up calendar with 'Open' tags / green dots on session days (tool-html.../default/1280-light.png, 375-light.png) and the deposit shown on every card; both are functional content rather than an identity layer, so they lift copy-level specificity but not the frame.
